name: DocumentDB (open-source, PostgreSQL-based)
tagline: MIT-licensed, MongoDB-compatible document engine built as PostgreSQL extensions, run by the Linux Foundation.
description: DocumentDB is an open-source document database that stores native BSON inside PostgreSQL through the pg_documentdb_core and pg_documentdb extensions, with a Rust gateway that speaks the MongoDB wire protocol. Microsoft open-sourced it in January 2025 as the engine behind Azure DocumentDB, then donated it to the Linux Foundation in August 2025; its steering committee now includes Microsoft, AWS, Rippling and Yugabyte. Version 1.0, the first GA release, shipped on 19 October 2026 alongside a 1.0 Kubernetes operator. It is the most credible permissively licensed path to MongoDB-compatible storage, and it inherits PostgreSQL's durability and tooling.
developer: DocumentDB project (Linux Foundation; originated at Microsoft)

pricing.notes: Free to self-host. Azure DocumentDB is the managed service built on it, and FerretDB 2.x used it as a backend.

scale.notes: Scales like a single PostgreSQL primary with streaming replicas; the operator handles HA and cross-cluster replication. Transparent sharding exists only in the Azure service today.

strengths: MIT license with vendor-neutral Linux Foundation governance
Works with existing MongoDB drivers and tools such as mongosh and Compass
Runs on stock PostgreSQL 15-18, so backups, replication and monitoring are familiar
Vector search via pgvector and text indexes built in
Backed by several cloud vendors, which makes it a likely common standard
weaknesses: Very young as a GA product (1.0 in October 2026); compatibility gaps remain
Change streams and some admin commands are incomplete
Performance tuning means understanding both PostgreSQL internals and MongoDB semantics
useCases: Migrating MongoDB apps onto PostgreSQL infrastructure
Document plus vector storage for RAG on Kubernetes
notIdealFor: Apps relying on the newest MongoDB-specific features
